facts.statement: Researchers initially debated whether Silesaurus was an early ornithischian, a basal sauropodomorph, or a non-dinosaur relative with similar adaptations.
facts.quote: Dzik revised his classification believing Silesaurus to be close to the origins of dinosaurs, either as an early ornithischian, an early member close to Ornithischia and Sauropodomorpha, or a closely related non-dinosaur showing similar adaptations for herbivory.

facts.statement: Silesaurus measured approximately 2.3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Silesaurus measured approximately 2.3 m in length.

facts.statement: Silesaurus was lightly built and likely a fast, agile animal with an active lifestyle.
facts.quote: Lightly built, it was probably a fast and agile animal with an active lifestyle.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the tip of Silesaurus's lower jaw was covered by a keratinous beak.
facts.quote: The tip of the dentary had no teeth, and evidence suggests that it was covered by a keratinous beak.

facts.statement: A 2019 study attributed fossil dung containing beetles to Silesaurus, suggesting it was not strictly a plant-eater.
facts.quote: A 2019 study by paleontologist Martin Qvarnström and colleagues examining coprolites (fossil dung) that contained beetles attributed them to Silesaurus based on size and other factors.

facts.statement: Silesaurus is often considered a quadruped that walked on all four legs thanks to its long, gracile forelimbs.
facts.quote: Silesaurus and silesaurids in general are often considered quadrupeds, walking on all four legs thanks to their long, gracile forelimbs.

facts.statement: There is an ongoing debate over whether Silesaurus was capable of bipedalism in some circumstances.
facts.quote: There is debate over whether they were capable of bipedalism (walking on only the hindlimbs) in some circumstances.

facts.statement: In 2020, researchers concluded that Silesaurus was likely an obligate quadruped based on its short hindlimbs and elongated forelimbs.
facts.quote: Piechowski and the paleontologist Mateusz Tałanda concluded in 2020 that the short hindlimbs combined with the elongated forelimbs supported the idea that it was an obligate (permanent) quadruped.

facts.statement: Fossils of Silesaurus were found in the Keuper Clay near Opole in Silesia, Poland, which is the origin of the species name.
facts.quote: Se encontraron unos 20 restos fósiles de Silesaurus en la Arcilla Keuper cerca de Opole, en Silesia (Polonia), lo que está en el origen del nombre de la especie.

facts.statement: The type species Silesaurus opolensis was described by Jerzy Dzik in 2003.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Silesaurus opolensis, fue descrito por Jerzy Dzik en 2003.

facts.statement: Silesaurus measured about 2.3 meters in length and was a facultative biped.
facts.quote: Silesaurus medía unos 2,3 metros de largo y era un bípedo facultativo.

facts.statement: Silesaurus was a herbivore.
facts.quote: Silesaurus era un herbívoro.

facts.statement: Most scientists believe Silesaurus was not a dinosaur but rather a dinosauriform.
facts.quote: La mayoría de los científicos piensan que Silesaurus no era un dinosaurio, sino más bien un dinosauriforme.

facts.statement: Silesaurus possesses some dinosaurian traits, such as a short iliac projection.
facts.quote: Silesaurus, tiene algunas características de dinosaurio, como: un saliente breve del ilion

facts.statement: According to alternative theories, Silesaurus occupies a position near the base of ornithischian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Como resultado, según las teorías alternativas, Silesaurus ocupa lugar en o cerca de la base de los dinosaurios ornitisquios.

facts.statement: Silesaurus belongs to the family Silesauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Silesauridae

facts.statement: Silesaurus is classified within the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Silesaurus lived during the Carnian stage, between 233.6 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (233.6 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Silesaurus was named by Dzik in 2003.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Silesaurus (genus), Dzik 2003

facts.statement: There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Silesaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 3

facts.statement: It is debated whether Silesaurus is a dinosaur or a dinosauriform, despite possessing features like a short iliac projection used for tail muscle attachment.
facts.quote: Sin embargo Silesaurus, tiene algunas características de dinosaurio, como: un saliente breve del ilion (una superficie ósea en el ilion que sirve de punto de sujeción para los músculos de la cola)

rejected.statement: Researchers hypothesized that Silesaurus's beak-like jaws were adapted for pecking small insects off the ground like modern birds.
rejected.quote: They hypothesized that the beak-like jaws were adapted for pecking small insects off the ground like modern birds.

rejected.quote: Pintore et al. (2021) found that the femur shape of Silesaurus overlapped with fully bipedal archosaurs rather than with quadrupeds.
